objective: Give the tests that start the CLI as a process a longer timeout on Windows only, since Windows runners are slow (maintainer: 'increase the timeout, windows is slow').
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-bump, branch release/0.3.1/chore/bump-version. It has an uncommitted diagnostic change in packages/integrations/pi/tests/session-context.test.ts from the previous Assignment: a per-child deadline CHILD_DEADLINE_MS of 20 s and PIPE_GRACE_MS of 2 s that kill a stalled child and report its arguments and partial output. Keep that diagnostic.

Evidence: on the Windows runner the suite takes 530-650 s, cold starts of the unbundled CLI (about 660 files) stall for long stretches, and the project-flag test in session-context.test.ts timed out even at 30 s (job 129267946040). stdin.test.ts took 29.9 s there against 3.6 s in an earlier run.

Add one shared constant for the timeout of tests that start the CLI or bundle as a process: 120_000 on win32 and 30_000 elsewhere. Follow the pattern cli.test.ts already uses for its win32 default (60_000), and put the constant where the tests can share it (an existing test helper module if one exists, otherwise a small new helper in each package's tests folder). Replace the 30_000 values added in the previous commit 5eb5f00 ('test: give the tests that start the CLI a 30 s timeout…', in version.test.ts, pipe.test.ts, session-context.test.ts, pi.test.ts, extension.test.ts and the setDefaultTimeout in hooks.test.ts) with that constant.

Scale the diagnostic CHILD_DEADLINE_MS so each of the two children may use nearly half the test's timeout (for example 55_000 on win32 and the current 20_000 elsewhere), so the diagnostic only fires before the test timeout and never cuts a slow but healthy run short.
